sections.text:
6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling
The PP/DS detailed scheduling heuristics and functions can be executed as part of the
production planning job and interactively from the detailed scheduling planning
board, the resource planning table, and the product planning table.
Apart from executing the heuristics in the background and in online mode to schedule
the operations on the resources, another important aspect of detailed scheduling is to
monitor the scheduling results from the scheduling tools and to adjust them to resolve
any issues found even after the scheduling runs.
During the heuristic execution, depending on the strategy settings, there could be
operations scheduled infinitely for dependent operations due to the error tolerance set
© 

399
6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling
in the strategy profile of the heuristics, or operations may be deallocated as part of the
heuristics. Such exceptions can be displayed from the detailed scheduling planning
board, and the production scheduler needs to schedule those operations.
With embedded PP/DS, new SAP Fiori apps are available to monitor the resource utili-
zation and change the shift schedule from the app itself to manage the resource capac-
ity. In addition, you can dispatch and deallocate operations on the resources and
simulate the results before the changes are saved in the system. The Advanced Sched-
uling Board SAP Fiori app is delivered in embedded PP/DS to perform detailed schedul-
ing activities. The Advanced Scheduling Board app has limited functionality compared
to the SAP GUI–based detailed scheduling planning board. However, the app contains
the functionalities required to execute and monitor basic scheduling. We’ll discuss
each of these execution options and apps in the following sections.

sections.title: Detailed Scheduling Planning Board
sections.text:
6.4.1 Detailed Scheduling Planning Board
The detailed scheduling planning board is one of the important tools production
schedulers use to visualize the schedule and adjust it by dragging and dropping opera-
tions onto the required resources on the timeline. Objects such as operations and
orders are color-coded to make it easy for schedulers to identify different objects based
on their status (e.g., scheduled operations vs. deallocated operations are displayed with
different colors and patterns). Graphical representation of the scheduling situation and
interactively simulating the resolution for the scheduling problems identified are the
main objectives when using the detailed scheduling planning board.
Multiple charts can be loaded onto the detailed scheduling planning board to display
the current scheduling satiation of the resources, the orders against the materials
loaded on the detailed scheduling planning board, stocks over time, and so on. These
charts can be switched on and off per the requirements from the detailed scheduling
planning board profiles and can be interactively changed in the detailed scheduling
planning board transaction itself.
The settings and the constraints maintained in the strategy profile are the core driving
the behavior of the interactive scheduling changes made on the detailed scheduling
planning board. You can save the adjusted schedule into a simulation version, which
later can be merged back into the active version by loading the simulation version onto
the detailed scheduling planning board and adopting it to the active version.
Planning Board Selection Screen
The detailed scheduling planning board can be launched via Transaction /SAPAPO/
CSPS0 or from SAP Easy Access menu, Logistics  Advanced Planning  Production Plan-
ning  Interactive Production Planning  Detailed Scheduling  Detailed Scheduling Plan-
ning Board – Variable View. The selection screen of the detailed scheduling planning
board is displayed in Figure 6.46.

6 Detailed Scheduling
400
Figure 6.46 Detailed Scheduling Planning Board: Selection Screen
The various profiles used in the detailed scheduling planning board, such as the
detailed scheduling strategy profile, heuristics profile, planning board profile, work
area, and propagation range, are assigned to the overall profile. (We’ve covered the
overall profile customization in Chapter 3, Section 3.6.1.) By assigning the Overall Pro-
file to the detailed scheduling planning board selection screen, all other relevant pro-
files are loaded per the customization.
The detailed scheduling planning board can be used for active planning version 000 or
for inactive planning versions. To use the detailed scheduling planning board to work
with the active planning version data, enter “000” in the Plng Version field.
The Time Profile assigned to the overall profile prefills the planning and display periods
in the selection screen, which can be manually overwritten. The display period is the
period for the duration used by the objects loaded onto the detailed scheduling plan-
ning board. But making changes to the schedule either by manually rescheduling or
© 

401
6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling
using a function or heuristics within the detailed scheduling planning board can only
be performed for the planning period defined in the selection screen.
Work Area is like a selection variant where the selection criteria for the resources, prod-
ucts, and orders are already entered and saved. Therefore, you, as a production sched-
uler, can create your own work area with the resources and products you’re responsible
for scheduling. The selection criteria filled in by the work area also can be overwritten
manually.
Tip
After changing the selection criteria for the resources, products, and orders, you can
save it to a new work area by clicking the Save button to the right of the Work Area
field on the selection screen.
In the Resource tab, set the Selected Resources checkbox to load only the resources
you’ve entered explicitly in the selection criteria, manually, or from the Work Area
definition. If you don’t set this indicator, the system will load additional resources
derived as follows:
 The selected resources and corresponding operations on the resource are loaded.
 From the operations, the orders are loaded, and from the orders, the system deter-
mines the other resources used by the orders (operations).
 From the operations and orders, the system loads the products in the product chart,
and the resources corresponding to other orders (operations) of the loaded products
are also displayed in the resource chart.
You should select the Selected Resources checkbox to ensure that the volume of data
loaded onto the detailed scheduling planning board is predictable and doesn’t lead to
poor performance of loading and subsequent processing of the detailed scheduling
planning board.
The same is applicable for the selection of materials entered in the Product tab of the
selection screen. Select the Selected Products checkbox to restrict the selection of prod-
ucts by the explicitly entered materials in the selection.
If the order/operation network display (pegging and order-internal relationship links)
is activated in the detailed scheduling planning board profile by not setting the check-
box in the No Display column for the Network View: Operations and Network View:
Orders, as shown in Figure 6.47, the selected resource or selected product setting is
ignored by the system, and the order network and corresponding resources and mate-
rials are loaded.
The detailed scheduling planning board performance is impacted by the volume of
data loaded and the number of charts loaded during start-up. To improve performance,
use time segments in the time profile definition so that the data is loaded in segments

6 Detailed Scheduling
402
as you work in the detailed scheduling planning board and navigate through the
resource time stream (scroll through the time scale). (Refer to Chapter 3, Section 3.6.2,
for more information on time segments.) The reading of the SAP liveCache data for the
display of the detailed scheduling planning board can be improved by selecting the
Perf.Func. checkbox. To select this checkbox, click on the Profiles button in the selec-
tion screen menu bar (refer to the top of Figure 6.46), and in the Plng Board Profile tab
of the popup screen, select the Perf.Func. checkbox on the bottom-left part of the
screen (see Figure 6.47).
You can hide the charts in the detailed scheduling planning board by setting the No
Display checkbox on the detailed scheduling planning board profile, as shown in Figure
6.47. After the right selection settings are made, click on the Execute button to load the
planning board.
Figure 6.47 Detailed Scheduling Planning Board Selection of Charts to Be Displayed, and
Setting the Performance Function
Planning Board Navigation
The detailed scheduling planning board, as shown in Figure 6.48, opens with the shuf-
fler on the left side of the screen, which has the list of resources under the Resource Pool
and a list of products under the Product Pool. You can display or hide resources and
products from the corresponding charts by selecting the resource and clicking on the
show or hide buttons in the shuffler 1. The shuffler can be hidden by clicking on the
Display/Hide Shuffler button on the menu bar 2.
© 

403
6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling
From the menu bar, you can navigate to the settings and perform actions such as
reschedule or deallocate selected operations. Manually performed scheduling changes
within the detailed scheduling planning board can be undone by using the Undo Last
Scheduling Function button in the menu bar. You can navigate to the menu bar path
More settings to manage all the settings for the display and function of the detailed
scheduling planning board, as shown in Figure 6.48.
Figure 6.48 Detailed Scheduling Planning Board: Navigation
Tip
If you want to change the detailed scheduling strategy profile, click on the DS Strategy
button in the menu bar. In the dialog popup for the strategy settings, click on the
Expert View on the bottom-right corner of the screen to display all available strategy
settings.
Depending of the average duration of the orders, you can set the granularity for the
timelines on the chart. If your orders are smaller (less than a day), you may set the time
scale as days; for working with resources with bigger orders, the time scale can be set to
weekly or monthly display. This can be changed from the menu bar settings, as well as
by right-clicking (context menu) on the time bar on the individual charts, as shown in
Figure 6.48 3. The toolbar 4 can be customized, which is covered in Chapter 3, Section
3.6.4.
Further additional settings for the detailed scheduling planning board display and
functions can be accessed by clicking on the More button in the menu bar and clicking
on the Settings option.

6 Detailed Scheduling
404
Context Menu
In the detailed scheduling planning board, many of the available functions for the
objects (resources, products, and operations/orders) are provided in the context menu
(right-click on the objects to access these menus).
You can click on the context menu of Resource to expand the display, as shown in Fig-
ure 6.49, if there is more than one order scheduled at the same time on the resource via
the Expand Multiple Loading option. You can also Define Downtimes on the resources
and create/change/delete fixing intervals with the Define Fixing Intervals option.
Figure 6.49 Resource Context Menu
On the product chart, the context menu provides options to navigate to production
planning transactions such as the product or pegging overview of the product. You can
load additional charts for displaying the product stock, and so on from the context
menu. The context menu of the orders and operation objects provides most of the pos-
sible actions for an order/operation.
Planning Board Features
The color and shape of the objects displayed in the detailed scheduling planning board
are configurable as covered in Chapter 3, Chapter 3.6.4. If you want to know what the
© 

405
6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling
object symbols represent, you can choose More  Extras  Legend. The legend lists the
charts and individual graphical objects, including the object and status they represent.
To manually move orders in the product chart or the operations in the resource chart,
you can click the operation/order, drag it to the desired position on the graphical rep-
resentation of the resource capacity, and drop it in position. If the detailed scheduling
strategy allows the operation/order to be placed in the desired position, it will be
placed there and scheduled according to the strategy profile (scheduling mode, direc-
tion, treatment of dependent operations, etc.).
To move multiple operations, as shown on the left side in Figure 6.50, you can press the
(Ctrl) key, select all the required operations, and drag them while the (Ctrl) key is still
pressed. Then release the dragged objects in the required position on the detailed
scheduling planning board. The current time stamp will be displayed on the bottom of
the screen. In addition, you can drag a box around the objects 1 by clicking to select
multiple objects, as shown in the left side of Figure 6.50.
When there are alternative modes present for the activities (alternative modes from
the same PDS), while selecting and dragging the operations manually, the system will
highlight the resource rows belonging to alternative modes in green 2, as shown on
the right side of Figure 6.50. This way, if there are capacity constraints in the primary
mode, you can place the operation on one of the highlighted alternative modes. If there
are alternative resources available from alternative PDSs, those aren’t highlighted.
Figure 6.50 Moving Operations and Alternative Modes
The pegging relationships between orders and inter-order relationships can be displayed
by choosing Extras  Activity/Pegging Relationships  Show. For individual objects, this

6 Detailed Scheduling
406
can be done from the context menu of the object. In Figure 6.51, you can see the fixed
pegging lines (dark red lines) 1, the dynamic pegging lines (green lines) 2, and the oper-
ation relationships lines (blue lines) 3. By double-clicking on the pegging links, you can
navigate to the pegging overview screen of the product view, where you can change the
type of pegging relationships if necessary.
Figure 6.51 Display of Pegging and Operations Relationships
The Alert Monitor can be invoked by clicking on the Alert Monitor button in the menu
bar or displaying the alerts by choosing More  Extras  Alerts  Display. This will high-
light the objects in the detailed scheduling planning board by making the object blink.
In the same menu path, the Hide option can be used to stop the display of alerts in the
chart objects. However, such graphics-intensive functions are performance intensive,
and they can be switched on and off only on a need basis and not set as default for reg-
ular usage of the detailed scheduling planning board.
Tip
To scroll on the timelines within the charts, you can use the arrow keys. If, after you’ve
selected objects and started scrolling, you want to cancel the action and place the
objects back in the original position, release the dragged objects on the time axis on
top of the chart. This will cancel the drag action.
You can use the Find button on the menu bar to search for objects with order number,
product, and so on. If you enter an order number and search, the system will highlight
all the operations of the order present in the resource chart and the order in the prod-
uct chart.
Execution of Functions
You can select one or multiple operations, orders, or resources to execute functions
such as rescheduling (according to the set strategy) or deallocating the objects. To exe-
cute a heuristic on the selected objects, select the objects (e.g., relevant resources), and
choose Functions  Heuristics, as shown in Figure 6.52. The heuristic you want to exe-
cute must be part of the heuristics profile you’ve assigned to the overall profile.
© 

407
6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling
Figure 6.52 Executing Heuristics from the Detailed Scheduling Planning Board
Unlike the interactive execution of production planning heuristics, most of the
detailed scheduling heuristics don’t have a dialog popup to change any heuristic set-
tings already saved in the heuristics. Only with the schedule sequence manually heu-
ristic (SAP003) is a new screen launched to list all the operations from the selected
resources for this heuristic, as shown in Figure 6.53. Here, you can move the operations
to the clipboard and sequence them manually (drag and drop between the Clipboard
side and Sequence to be planned side). After you set the sequence for the operations,
click on the Schedule button. The operations will be scheduled based on the strategy
profile set in the heuristic.
Figure 6.53 Schedule Sequence Manually Heuristic
To check the logs of the actions performed in the detailed scheduling planning board,
you can click on the Logs button in the menu bar. This will display all the planning and
scheduling logs generated from manual actions as well as the heuristics executions.

6 Detailed Scheduling
408
Simulation Session
All the schedule changes and the heuristics you executed in the detailed scheduling
planning board are always performed in a simulation session (sim session) by the sys-
tem, until you adopt the changes to the active version while saving. When you navigate
back from the detailed scheduling planning board screen, the system prompts for you
to Adopt the current scheduling data from the detailed scheduling planning board into
the active planning version or to Save the data to a simulation version, which can be
worked on later before merging back to the active version, as shown in Figure 6.54.
Figure 6.54 Detailed Scheduling Planning Board: Option to Save the Data in a
Simulation Version
Note
The simulation version saved from the detailed scheduling planning board scheduling
data shouldn’t be confused with the inactive planning versions, which can be created
by copying the active planning version 000. These are two different objects. The simu-
lation version from the detailed scheduling planning board only has the data loaded
onto the planning board. Inactive planning versions (copy of 000) are created and
maintained from the version copy report and Transaction /SAPAPO/MVM (Model Ver-
sion Management).
When merging the simulation version data or the data from the detailed scheduling
planning board session (sim session) back with the active version, the merge will take
place depending on the status of the objects. For example, if you’ve rescheduled an
operation of a production order in the detailed scheduling planning board, and the
order has been confirmed in SAP S/4HANA in the meantime, then while merging the
sim session (rescheduled operation) to the active version (operation confirmed), the
status in the active version takes higher priority, and the rescheduling change from the
detailed scheduling planning board will be ignored during the merge. While working in
the detailed scheduling planning board, you can perform a refresh to load the current
© 

409
6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling
active version data onto the planning board; this overwrites any changes you’ve made
so far in the detailed scheduling planning board.
The simulation versions can be accessed from Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSS0, as shown
in Figure 6.55. The saved simulation sessions can be loaded onto the detailed schedul-
ing planning board (graphical processing 1) or to the resource planning table (tabular
processing 2). In addition, from this transaction, the simulation version can be
adopted to the active version 3.
Figure 6.55 Accessing Simulation Versions
Multilevel Time Buffers
A multilevel time buffer (MLTB) calculates the buffer for rescheduling orders without
impacting the schedule of the upstream or downstream orders in the pegging struc-
ture. This is useful in situations where a finished product is produced in a constrained
resource with many products scheduled on it. If a change is required in the semifin-
ished product’s order schedule, it would eventually impact the finished product’s man-
ufacturing resources, which has far more impact due to the line manufacturer’s
multiple other products. In this case, if there is a time gap between the finished product
and semifinished product orders, the MLTB calculates this exact time gap and displays
it as a key figure in the planning board. This will help the schedulers with a time thresh-
old within which the semifinished order can be rescheduled without impacting the
schedule of the finished product order scheduled on the constrained resource.
There are three types of time buffers that can be calculated and displayed in the plan-
ning board:
 Time buffer relative to successor
This is the time difference between the operation being rescheduled and the imme-
diate next operation of the same order or the next order that is pegged to the opera-
tion/order being rescheduled.
 Time buffer relative to predecessor
This is the time difference between the operation being rescheduled and the imme-
diate previous operation of the same order or the next order that is pegged to the
operation/order being rescheduled.

6 Detailed Scheduling
410
 Time buffer relative to primary demand
The primary demand is the top level of the pegging structure, which can be a forecast
requirement, sales order requirement, and so on. If there are gaps between the oper-
ations of the orders and gaps between the orders, the time buffer relative to primary
demand for any level of the order/operation in the pegging structure is the total
time that becomes available if all these gaps are closed. The primary demand date is
a constant. The orders/operations will be simulated with an infinite backward sched-
uling starting at the demand due date till the operation/order for which this key fig-
ure is being calculated and that value is displayed.
In the example shown in Figure 6.56, the top portion A is the original schedule of the
orders on their resources. Here, we’ll take the order 1 for product S4PPDS_MLTB_
HALB1, which is pegged to the higher level and pegged by a lower-level material, as an
example and see how the buffers are calculated. For calculating the time buffer relative
to the successor, the system calculates the difference 2 between the end time stamp of
this order and the start time stamp of the higher-level pegged order (for product
S4PPDS_MLTB_FERT1).
Figure 6.56 Example for Calculation of Time Buffers Relative to Predecessor and Successor
Orders
As shown in the middle part of the screen B, if the order is manually rescheduled
within this calculated threshold, this doesn’t impact the schedule of the higher-level
order. Similarly, the difference 3 between the start time stamp of the order 1 and the
end time stamp of the lower-level order pegged (for product S4PPDS_MLTB_HALB2)
provides the time buffer relative to predecessor. As you can see in the bottom part of
Figure 6.56 C, moving the order in the backward direction within the buffer threshold
won’t impact the schedule of the order for product S4PPDS_MLTB_HALB2.
© 

411
6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling
An example of the time buffer relative to the primary demand is shown in Figure 6.57.
The original schedule is shown in the top portion A. Here the time buffer relative to pri-
mary demand is being calculated for the order in the lowest level of the pegging struc-
ture. The primary demand is a forecast element 2. For this order 1, the system
calculates the difference 3 of the end time of the order (for which the buffer is being
calculated) and the end time of the same order, if it’s rescheduled along with all orders
in the higher pegging levels (with no gaps) and without impacting the due date for the
primary demand 2, as shown in the bottom part B.
Figure 6.57 Example of Calculation of Time Buffer Relative to Primary Demand
The time buffer can be calculated as a gross duration or as net duration. For example, if
an operation is disturbed by a nonworking day or shift break, the gross duration is the
difference of the start and end time stamps of the operation. The net duration is the
actual operation duration, which doesn’t include the nonworking times. The MLTB Pro-
file determines whether the duration calculated in the gross or net duration. The MLTB
profile can be configured using SAP IMG menu path, SPRO  Advanced Planning 
Detailed Scheduling  Maintain MLTB Profiles. In the MLTB profile settings, under the
Time Buffer Calculation Method field, you can set if the duration needs to be calculated
in net time or gross time, as shown in Figure 6.58.
In the detailed scheduling planning board, you can set the overall profile SAP_MLTB to
display the MLTB-related key figures such as the buffer relative to successor/predeces-
sor in the order and operation charts in the detailed scheduling planning board. After
entering this overall profile and the selection criteria for the detailed scheduling plan-
ning board, execute the transaction, and you’ll be in the detailed scheduling planning
board. Within the detailed scheduling planning board, select the resources (see Figure
6.59 1) for which you want to calculate the time buffers for the corresponding orders
and operations. Then navigate to Functions  Multi-Level Time Buffer  Calculate Time
Buffer 2. This will calculate the time buffer key figures, and in the order chart 3 and
operations chart 4, you can see the values for the buffers updated. When there are
changes made to the schedule of the orders, you can use the Refresh Time Buffer 5 to
recalculate the buffers based on the new scheduling situation.

6 Detailed Scheduling
412
Figure 6.58 MLTB Profile Settings
Figure 6.59 Calculation and Display of Multilevel Time Buffer in Detailed Scheduling Planning
Board
© 

413

sections.text:
6.4.2 Advanced Scheduling Board
In embedded PP/DS, Advanced Scheduling Board is delivered as a standard SAP Fiori
app. This app can be used to perform order-scheduling functions such as schedule,
deallocate, fix, interrupt, creation/deletion of orders, setting conversion indicator for
planned orders, and so on. The Alert Monitor is integrated to this app. In addition, exe-
cution of detailed scheduling heuristics is also possible through the Advanced Schedul-
ing Board app.
Note
The Advanced Scheduling Board is a new SAP Fiori app. The old Production Scheduling
Board app is still available as of SAP S/4HANA 2022, but all the new features and func-
tionalities are delivered in the new Advanced Scheduling Board app.
Activation of advanced planning (PP/DS) is mandatory for using the Advanced Sched-
uling Board app, and only the resources activated for advanced planning can be sched-
uled via the app.
This SAP Fiori app is delivered with the authorization business role SAP_BR_PRODN_PLNR.
After your user is assigned a role, the Advanced Scheduling Board app appears under
the Advanced Planning tab in the SAP Fiori launchpad, as shown in Figure 6.60.
Figure 6.60 Advanced Scheduling Board App in the SAP Fiori Launchpad
To activate the Advanced Scheduling Board app, the backend OData service needs to be
registered and maintained in the SAP S/4HANA system. To register the service, use
Transaction /IWBEP/CONF_SERVICE. As shown in Figure 6.61, in this transaction, enter
the value “UI_SCM_ADVNCD_SCHEDG_BOARD” for the Service and enter “1” in the
Service Version field. Execute the transaction, and in the next screen, select the Deacti-
vate Parallelization of Batch Requests checkbox and save the transaction. This is a tech-
nical setting required for certain types of SAP Fiori apps.

6 Detailed Scheduling
414
Figure 6.61 Registration of OData Service for the Advanced Scheduling Board App
Like the MRP apps, the Advanced Scheduling Board app also works based on the area of
responsibility (AOR). For the Advanced Scheduling Board app, the AOR is the combina-
tion of the plant and the planner assigned to the resource master data. When you
launch the app for the first time, you’ll see a popup to set up the AOR. Subsequent to
changing the AOR, click on the user profile button within the Advanced Scheduling
Board app, and select the App Settings option, as shown in Figure 6.62. In the App Set-
tings popup screen, click on the Area of Responsibility. In the resulting screen, click on
the Add Plant and Planner 1 button to assign new planners and plant combinations to
the AOR. Use the Delete 2 button to remove existing assignments.
Once you launch the app, you’ll see the default filter options such as the display hori-
zon and the resource name. To add additional filters, click on Adapt Filters, and you’ll
see a list of all available filter options, as shown in Figure 6.63. Select the required filter
options, and you can save the added filters and values you’ve entered for the filter val-
ues as a variant.
© 

415
6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling
Figure 6.62 Setting Up Area of Responsibility in the Advanced Scheduling Board App
Figure 6.63 Filter Options in the Advanced Scheduling Board App
In the charts selection dropdown 1, you can select the charts to be loaded on the
Advanced Scheduling Board app. A maximum of four different charts can be selected
and loaded at one time, as shown in Figure 6.64.

6 Detailed Scheduling
416
Figure 6.64 Chart Selection Options in Advanced Scheduling Board
Display Horizon is a mandatory filter field where you can choose from options such as
current year, quarter, month, or a date range. After the filter options are entered and
the charts to be displayed are selected, click on the Go button to load the charts with the
corresponding graphical objects. In the top of the screen shown in Figure 6.65 is the
selection filter bar 1 and the toolbar 2 with various options to execute detailed sched-
uling steps in the Advanced Scheduling Board app. All the displayed charts have a table
area 3 where you can set additional details for the corresponding object such as
resources, products, or orders, depending on the chart.
Figure 6.65 Advanced Scheduling Board App Details
© 

417
6.4 Triggering PP/DS Scheduling
Click on the Settings button 4 within the chart table area to select the columns to be
displayed in the table. In the graphical chart area 5, the graphical elements such as
operations and orders are displayed, depending on the charts loaded.
In the toolbar shown in Figure 6.66, click on the Settings button 1, and in the Profile
Settings tab in the Settings popup, you can enter the Alert Profile. Once the alert profile
is entered, click on the Alerts button 2 to display the list of alerts generated per the
alert profile settings. In the Alerts popup, use the dropdown 3 to select the alert type to
display the alert list. In the list of alerts, click on the Go To 4 button to highlight the cor-
responding object 5 in the graphical chart area.
Figure 6.66 Alert Monitor in the Advanced Scheduling Board App
In the resource chart to display overlapped operations on the resources, as shown in
Figure 6.67, click on the Expand Overlap button 1 to display operations that are loaded
in parallel on the resources. You can select multiple objects by holding down the (Ctrl)
button or by dragging a box around the objects to be selected. With the objects
selected, click on the Show Relationships/Pegging Relationships button in the toolbar
2 to display the operation relationships and the order pegging relationships 3 in the
corresponding charts. The Scheduling button in the toolbar helps to execute simple
scheduling functions 4 such as Fix, Undo Fix, Deallocate, and Reschedule operations.
Click on the Go to Date button 5 to select a specific date from a calendar popup to nav-
igate to a specific date in the graphical chart area.
The Zoom In, Zoom Out, and the Zoom Slider 6 buttons can be used to control the gran-
ularity of the time periods such as days, weeks, months, and so on, displayed in the
graphical chart area. Click on the Find button 7, which will open a popup 8 to search
and highlight objects within the graphical chart areas.

6 Detailed Scheduling
418
Figure 6.67 Features within the Advanced Scheduling Board App
As shown in Figure 6.68, there are context menu options available both on the objects
in the table area and on the graphical objects. For options in context menus such as
order processing or resource master data, the corresponding GUI transaction is ren-
dered in an HTML screen. The context menu options in the resources 1 and the opera-

sections.title: Detailed Scheduling Optimizer
sections.text:
6.5 Detailed Scheduling Optimizer
The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer is an optional component of embedded PP/DS. The
main purpose of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer is to create a mathematical model
of the scheduling problems and resolve them by reducing the weighted objective func-
tions associated with the scheduling problem, such as makespan (total lead time) of the
operations on the resources, setup time, setup cost, delay cost, and mode cost. The
Detailed Scheduling Optimizer also respects the hard constraints provided and will
attempt to respect the soft constraints. The result is a schedule that is optimized per the
objective functions defined in the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile.
The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer can be executed from the detailed scheduling tools
such as the detailed scheduling planning board and product planning table. In addi-
tion, you can schedule the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer execution as a part of the
background production planning run as a planning step.
The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer engine is installed in one of the application servers
of the SAP S/4HANA system or in a separate server. TCP/IP is set up between the SAP
S/4HANA system and the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer server. When Detailed
Scheduling Optimizer is executed from the PP/DS tools, the data is collected from SAP
liveCache and from the PP/DS application, and then the data is sent along with the
Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile settings. Detailed Scheduling Optimizer creates
the optimal plan by executing multiple iterations of the solution and sending the final
solution back to embedded PP/DS. The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer settings are
maintained in the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile from Customizing menu
path, SAP IMG Menu  Advanced Planning  Detailed Scheduling  Maintain Optimiza-
tion Profiles, or from Customizing Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSC5. The list of optimiza-
tion profiles is displayed in this transaction, as shown in Figure 6.82.
Figure 6.82 Optimization Profiles
Double-clicking on an optimization profile will take you to the screen with the optimi-
zation profile details, as shown in Figure 6.83.
© 

431
6.5 Detailed Scheduling Optimizer
Figure 6.83 Optimization Profile: Details
We’ll cover the important settings under the different tabs of the optimization profile
in the following sections. The objective functions are the main drivers of the Detailed
Scheduling Optimizer functionality, so we’ll cover the details of the objective functions
before covering the critical settings on the different tabs.

sections.title: Objective Functions
sections.text:
6.5.1 Objective Functions
The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer works based on the objective functions and the val-
ues defined against the objective functions, such as delay cost, mode cost, and so on.
The objective functions are defined in the Basic Settings tab of the Detailed Scheduling
Optimizer profile.
The following objective functions are supported by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer,
as shown in Figure 6.84:
 Makespan
Makespan is the total lead time. This is the time difference between the earliest start
date of the optimized schedule and the end of the last unfixed operation in the hori-
zon for which the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer is being executed. The Detailed
Scheduling Optimizer decreases the makespan by reducing any gaps between the

6 Detailed Scheduling
432
operations or by resequencing orders so that the orders aren’t impacted by breaks in
the resource. When a weightage value is provided for the makespan, the value for the
objective function is calculated as follows:
Weighted makespan = Weightage for makespan in profile × Makespan in seconds
Figure 6.84 Objective Functions in Detailed Scheduling Optimizer
 Total Setup Times
When sequence-dependent setup activities are involved in scheduling, the detailed
scheduling heuristics can’t optimize the schedule by calculating the setup times in
iterations to schedule the operations in the optimal sequence. In such scenarios, the
Total Setup Times objective function can be set with a higher weightage value so that
the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer will reduce the total setup time required for all
the operations within the optimization horizon by resequencing the operations. The
weighted total setup time is calculated as follows:
Weighted total setup time = Weightage for setup time in profile × Total setup times of
all the operations in the optimization horizon
 Total Setup Costs
Similar to the setup times, the relative setup costs are also defined in the setup
matrix master data. Especially if the changeovers are based on multiple characteris-
tics and generated setup matrices based on characteristics are used, the number of
changeovers is high, and the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer can help reduce the
setup costs. Figure 6.85 shows an example of the generated setup matrix based on
© 

433
6.5 Detailed Scheduling Optimizer
characteristics. The generated setup matrices based on characteristics can be
accessed from Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPS_CHARMAT.
The time unit of measure maintained in the setup matrix is converted into an equiv-
alent time unit of measure of seconds for consideration by the Detailed Scheduling
Optimizer weighted objective value. The setup cost is a relative cost—not the actual
cost—and no unit of measure or currency is maintained nor conversion applied
when calculating the weighted setup cost totals.
Figure 6.85 Generated Setup Matrix with Setup Times and Setup Costs
 Maximum Delay Costs/Total Delay Costs
The maximum delay and total delay costs are calculated from the delay in seconds.
The delay in delivering a requirement is derived by calculating the requirement date
and the assigned receipt elements receipt date and then converting it into seconds.
The requirement priority drives the delay costs; that is, the higher the priority (1 is
higher), the higher is the delay cost. The list of Delay Costs up to a certain priority is
defined in the Costs tab of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile, as shown in
Figure 6.86. The delay costs are calculated as follows:
Total delay cost = Total of ((Delay for the order in seconds) × (Weightage maintained in
the profile) × (Delay cost for the priority of the order))

6 Detailed Scheduling
434
 Total Mode Costs
When alternative modes are available to manufacture a material, the cost of using
different modes can be reduced as an objective function using the Detailed Schedul-
ing Optimizer. In general, the higher the mode priority (A is the highest priority), the
lesser is the mode cost. The mode cost is calculated as follows:
Total mode cost = Fixed costs + (Variable costs × Duration of activity in seconds)
The mode costs are also maintained in the Costs tab of the Detailed Scheduling Opti-
mizer profile, as shown in Figure 6.86. In Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSC5, from the list
of all PP/DS optimization profiles, double-click the profile you want to change, and
navigate to the Costs tab to maintain the mode and delay costs.
Figure 6.86 Mode Costs and Order Priority Costs in the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Profile
The constraints for the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer can be configured within the
optimization profile, which we’ll discuss in the next section. However, certain con-
straints, such as resource availability (working times, utilization percentage), are hard
constraints and can’t be changed in the optimization profile.

sections.title: Optimization Profile
sections.text:
6.5.2 Optimization Profile
We’ve covered the objective functions and cost definition in the optimization profile in
the previous section. Now, we’ll discuss some of the other important settings in the
Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile.
Basic Settings
Let’s start with the Basic Settings tab, as shown in Figure 6.87, which includes the fol-
lowing key settings:
© 

435
6.5 Detailed Scheduling Optimizer
 Maximum Runtime
Depending on the volume of data involved and the complexity of the scheduling
problems, the runtime for the optimization can vary. The Detailed Scheduling Opti-
mizer will keep iterating the solutions to further reduce the objective functions and
to find the best possible solution. After a certain number of iterations, you may
observe from the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer logs that the runtime required to
perform these iterations isn’t worth the reduction in the objective function values.
In this case, you can define a maximum runtime for the Detailed Scheduling Opti-
mizer, so that it will end the iteration at the defined maximum runtime and save the
best solution found so far.
Figure 6.87 Optimizer Profile: Basic Settings
 Backwards Scheduling
Backwards scheduling is a follow-on step after the optimization to bring orders closer
to the requirements. The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer may schedule orders too
early to reduce the objective functions defined; in those cases, backwards scheduling
can be executed by selecting the Backwards Scheduling checkbox under the Addi-
tional Strategies area so that the orders are scheduled closer to the requirement dates.
Executing backwards scheduling may result in gaps between the operations, which
can be avoided by selecting the Compact Scheduling checkbox in this same area.

6 Detailed Scheduling
436
Order Processing
In the Order Processing tab, shown in Figure 6.88, you define the options for the order
categories of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer run and settings based on the status of
the orders and operations. The Other Manufacturing Levels settings determine whether
the pegging relationships of the higher level and lower level orders in the pegging struc-
ture and their relationship to the order being optimized need to be considered as a sec-
ondary constraint by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer. If you select the Ignore
Upstream Orders and/or Do Not Consider Subsequent Orders checkboxes, the Detailed
Scheduling Optimizer schedule may look optimized, but the material flow in terms of
pegging relationships can be broken. In a combined Production Planning Optimizer and
Detailed Scheduling Optimizer run using the Production Planning Optimizer (/SAPAPO/
PPO_OPT), the system dynamically updates the order validity dates for the operations
that are to be scheduled within a bucket. So, in the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile
that is to be assigned in the Production Planning Optimizer execution, it’s required to
set the Validity Periods of Orders as at least a soft constraint. So that the system respects
the Production Planning Optimizer–supplied order validity dates for the operations to
be optimized by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer.
Figure 6.88 Optimizer Profile: Order Processing Settings
© 

437
6.5 Detailed Scheduling Optimizer
Resource Processing
In the Resource Processing tab of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile, as shown
in Figure 6.89, the handling of capacities and scheduling relationship parameters and
constraints are set for the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer.
Figure 6.89 Resource Processing Settings in the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Profile
When calendar resources are used, they are assigned to the location master data as
inbound handling resources for scheduling goods receipt (GR) times of the orders.
There is no capacity consumption with the usage of calendar resources, and these
resources are only used for scheduling the GR activities. When there are orders in the
optimization horizon with activities that use calendar resources, then how the Detailed
Scheduling Optimizer handles such activities is set under the Non-Selected Calendar
Resources area of the Resource Processing tab. If the calendar resources are selected as
part of the resource selection for optimization, these settings aren’t relevant. When
you select Activities Are Fixed, the system reschedules the product activity of the order,
but the GR activity stays where it was before the optimization, thus impacting the over-
all duration of the order.

6 Detailed Scheduling
438
Resource Capacity Load settings control which resources are finitely scheduled during the
optimization run. With the selection of Always Schedule as Finite, all the relevant
resources being optimized will be scheduled finitely. The resource master data setting Rel-
evant for Finite Scheduling isn’t considered, and irrespective of the resource master data
setting, the resource will be finitely scheduled by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer.
The Lowest Mode Priority setting, which the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer can select
from alternative modes, is defined under the Mode Priority section. The Lower Priority
Modes setting directs Detailed Scheduling Optimizer behavior when there are activi-
ties with proprieties lower than the lowest mode priority allowed to be selected by the
Detailed Scheduling Optimizer. The system can choose a higher priority mode when
you select Choose a different mode from the Lower Priority Modes dropdown.
Horizon
In the Horizon tab of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile, the Start of the Optimi-
zation Horizon and the End of Optimization Horizon options are set. Options are avail-
able to set these dates relative to the current date. The relative dates work better when
running the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer as part of the production planning run as a
batch job because there is no manual intervention required to change the dates for
every job. Start of the Optimized Plan is the date/time from which the system can start
scheduling the optimized orders and operations on the resources.
During optimization, the operations that lie entirely within the optimization horizon
are considered for rescheduling. The handling of the orders that lie partially within the
optimization horizon is defined in the Order Processing tab under the Orders Partially
Located Outside the Optimization Horizon section.
Note
The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer in embedded PP/DS can’t create new orders to ful-
fill any open demand. This is only possible in the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer in the
standalone PP/DS component of SAP Advanced Planning and Optimization.
Additional Strategies
The Decomposition setting in the Additional Strategies tab is used to split the schedul-
ing problems into multiple smaller problems so that the Detailed Scheduling Opti-
mizer can efficiently solve smaller problems. Don’t switch on the decomposition to
just improve the performance of the optimization run because the quality of the plan-
ning results may be affected by switching on the decomposition.
Any increase in the makespan due to the backwards scheduling can be controlled and
avoided by selecting the Do Not Increase Makespan checkbox in the Backwards Schedul-
ing section of the Additional Strategies tab. With this setting, the previously optimized
makespans of the orders are protected from any change due to backwards scheduling.
© 

439
6.5 Detailed Scheduling Optimizer
Expert Settings
The Expert Settings tab of the profile, as shown in Figure 6.90, has the settings related
to logging the messages generated during the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer run. The
Explain Result option will write an explanation log on the changes the operations and
orders have gone through during the optimization. Log Result and Log Interim Solution
will log the resulting objective function values and the value of the objective functions
during the iterations performed by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer.
Figure 6.90 Expert Settings for Logging and Parallel Processing in the Detailed Scheduling
Optimizer Profile
Parallel Processing is an important aspect of improving Detailed Scheduling Optimizer
performance. But the sizing of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer server should be per-
formed to handle such parallel processing workloads. The number of slots that can be
used by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer is defined in the connection properties in
Transaction RCC_CUST. The number of parallel processes defined in the Max. No. of
Parallel Processes field should be less than the number of slots available for the
Detailed Scheduling Optimizer.

6 Detailed Scheduling
440

sections.title: Execute and Monitor Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Runs
sections.text:
6.5.3 Execute and Monitor Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Runs
The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer can be executed interactively from the detailed
scheduling planning board or from the product planning table. You can also run the
Detailed Scheduling Optimizer as a background job via the production planning run. In
this section, we’ll walk through each execution option.
Detailed Scheduling Optimizer in the Planning Run
After materials planning with MRP heuristics and, if required, aligning the receipt and
requirement elements with a heuristic (e.g., top-down or bottom-up heuristics), the
Detailed Scheduling Optimizer can be executed to schedule the orders finitely on the
critical resources and to optimize the schedule.
Figure 6.91 Optimization in the Production Planning Run: New Variant Creation
© 

441
6.5 Detailed Scheduling Optimizer
The optimization is available in the production planning run as a function, which isn’t
a heuristic. The heuristics are defined using an algorithm in the heuristics customiza-
tion (Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSC11), but the functions, such as the optimization,
aren’t listed in the heuristics list in the Customizing transaction; instead, they are listed
as a function to be selected in the planning run transaction. The global parameters,
such as Planning Version, Time Profile, and Propagation Range, need to be set as shown
in Figure 6.91. The optimization function takes only the resources as the object selec-
tion. The optimization can be one of the planning steps in the production planning run
after the MRP steps (refer to Chapter 5, Section 5.6), or a separate variant can be created
for the optimization through the planning run in Transaction /SAPAPO/CDPSB1 and
can be scheduled as an independent job.
Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Execution from the Detailed Scheduling Planning Board
From the detailed scheduling planning board, the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer can
be executed for the resources selected as part of the detailed scheduling planning
board. The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile settings can be changed interactively
in the detailed scheduling planning board before executing the optimization. As
Detailed Scheduling Optimizer execution from the detailed scheduling planning board
is done in dialog/online mode, it’s recommended to have a smaller value entered for
the Maximum Runtime for Detailed Scheduling Optimizer in the settings to avoid any
timeout situation.
Let’s walk through the following steps to execute the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer
from the detailed scheduling planning board:
1. Click on the Optimize button in the menu bar.
2. In the next screen, shown in Figure 6.92, set the Date/Time for the Start of Horizon
and End of Horizon for optimization and the Date/Time for the Start of Optimized
Schedule. Make sure the orders and operations you optimize are within the optimi-
zation horizon. Operations outside the horizon are considered fixed for optimiza-
tion. Click Continue to arrive at the optimization screen.
Figure 6.92 Horizon Settings for Optimization

6 Detailed Scheduling
442
3. Click on the Optimization Profile button 1 (see Figure 6.93) on the optimization
screen to navigate to the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile settings 2. After
making any adjustments to the profile, click on the Copy button 3 to save the values
for the current Detailed Scheduling Optimizer run.
4. Click on the Execute button to start the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer run 4.
Figure 6.93 Accessing Optimizer Settings from the Interactive Detailed Scheduling Optimizer
Execution
The list of resources selected for the optimization can be displayed from the Detailed
Scheduling Optimizer screen by clicking on the Display Resource List button.
The reduction in the objective values over time of the optimization is interactively
shown in a graphical format. After the optimization is completed, the logs, results, and
explanation logs are written if the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile has the rele-
vant settings in the Expert Settings tab. The messages generated during the Detailed
Scheduling Optimizer run with the statistical information about the resources and
activities are displayed on the Optimization screen, as shown in Figure 6.94.
© 

443
6.5 Detailed Scheduling Optimizer
Figure 6.94 Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Interactive Execution and Results
The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer finds an initial solution and then keeps iterating
the solution to find better solutions. If End Run after First Solution is set in the Detailed
Scheduling Optimizer profile settings (Basic Settings tab), the Detailed Scheduling
Optimizer will stop after the initial solution is found.
The Absolute Values button adjusts the solution process graph to show the total value
of the objective function calculated. Switching the display to Weighted Values shows
the objective function parameter values by applying the weightage defined in the
Detailed Scheduling Optimizer profile. The current solution values are also displayed in
the screen, as shown in Figure 6.94.
The Detailed Scheduling Optimizer Log (see Figure 6.95) collects runtime (performance)
information of the individual steps of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer run, includ-
ing the reading of parameters for the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer, loading the data
from SAP liveCache, executing the genetic algorithm in the Detailed Scheduling Opti-

All the activities rescheduled by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer are listed in the
Reschedulings tab of the explanation log. In addition, the interim solutions (the reduc-
tion in the objective functions) that the system calculated are shown in the Solutions

In the Sol. (solution) tab of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer output (refer to Figure

Monitoring Background Optimizer Runs
When the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer is scheduled as a background job from the
production planning run, you can use Transaction /SAPAPO/OPT11 (RCCF [remote con-
trol and communication framework] Log Display) to monitor the Detailed Scheduling
Optimizer execution status and results. The same transaction can also be used to ana-
lyze the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer runs executed interactively by users from the
detailed scheduling planning board, the product planning table, or any other applica-
tions.
The RCCF log display tool displays all the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer executions, as
shown in Figure 6.98. The Appl. column displays the value DPS for the Detailed Sched-
uling Optimizer execution and PPO for the Production Planning Optimizer execution.
From the list of Detailed Scheduling Optimizer executions, you can click the Log icon
under the Mess. Log column to display the application logs with the runtime distribu-
tion. Click the magnifying glass icon under Ext.Column to open the explanation log for
that execution, as shown in Figure 6.98.

If you want to terminate the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer execution that is currently
running in the system, you can use Transaction /SAPAPO/OPT_STOP (RCCF Active Ses-

Optimizer, you observe that the objective functions aren’t reduced after a point in
time, and you want to save the solution as of that point and terminate the Detailed
Scheduling Optimizer run. To do a graceful termination, where the latest solution is
saved and sessions are terminated by the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer, you can use
the Stop Process button, after selecting the current Detailed Scheduling Optimizer ses-

6.6 Summary
In this chapter, we’ve covered the detailed scheduling functions and tools in embedded
PP/DS. For scheduling in PP/DS, the strategy settings are critical to ensure the schedule
is set per the shop floor setup and requirements. We’ve covered in detail the function-
ality and working of various aspects of the strategy settings, including the scheduling
modes, scheduling direction, cross-order relationships, and order-internal relation-
ships.
The same strategy settings are also applied within many of the detailed scheduling
heuristics. We’ve covered the basic detailed scheduling heuristics to perform functions
such as sequencing, resolving backlogs, and scheduling deallocated operations. The
multilevel scheduling framework heuristics, including the stable forward scheduling
heuristic, were also covered in detail in this chapter. The multiresource scheduling heu-
ristic can be used to schedule operations on alternative modes, including modes from
alternative sources of supply (PDSs). We covered the DDMRP-based prioritized schedul-
ing for DDMRP planned products.
The detailed scheduling heuristics can be executed via background jobs in the produc-
tion planning run as well as in interactive mode. We’ve also covered the interactive
detailed scheduling tools, such as the detailed scheduling planning board, the Advanced

6 Detailed Scheduling
448
Scheduling Board app, the Monitor Capacity Utilization app, and the resource planning
table. We covered the concept of the multilevel time buffers in the detailed scheduling
planning board section of this chapter.
The important settings, functionalities, and workings of the Detailed Scheduling Opti-
mizer and the monitoring of the Detailed Scheduling Optimizer runs were also dis-
cussed in this chapter.
We’ve covered the monitoring of the production planning and detailed scheduling
applications via the jobs and logs of those application executions. From the business
process perspective, it’s important to monitor the accuracy of planning and schedul-
ing. The Alert Monitor tool is used for monitoring the accuracy of the plan and sched-
ule, as well as to proactively monitor for any supply chain issues. We’ll cover the Alert
Monitor in the next chapter.
